avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium forms insoluble complexes with iron, reducing iron absorption by up to 50%
avoid_supplements.action: Separate dosing by at least 2 hours; take iron supplements 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium acetate

avoid_supplements.name: Zinc supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium competitively inhibits zinc absorption in the GI tract
avoid_supplements.action: Administer zinc supplements at least 2 hours apart from calcium acetate dosing

avoid_supplements.name: Fluoride supplements/sodium fluoride
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium binds fluoride in GI tract, reducing fluoride bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2-4 hours

avoid_supplements.name: Tetracycline antibiotics (oral)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium chelates tetracyclines, significantly reducing antibiotic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; administer tetracyclines 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium acetate

avoid_supplements.name: Quinolone antibiotics (oral)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium reduces quinolone absorption and bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Separate dosing by at least 2 hours

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Vitamin D increases calcium absorption; combined use enhances efficacy but requires monitoring for hypercalcemia in susceptible patients
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum calcium levels; dose adjustment may be necessary

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: High calcium can reduce magnesium absorption; may lead to magnesium depletion with chronic use
caution_supplements.action: Monitor magnesium levels; maintain adequate spacing between doses if possible

avoid_foods.name: High-phosphorus foods (dairy, nuts, seeds, legumes)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Calcium acetate's primary mechanism is phosphate binding; high dietary phosphorus reduces therapeutic efficacy in hyperphosphatemia management
avoid_foods.action: Implement strict dietary phosphorus restriction as part of renal disease management; coordinate with dietitian

caution_foods.name: Spinach, kale, and high-oxalate vegetables
caution_foods.mechanism: Oxalates bind calcium, reducing calcium availability; generally minimal clinical impact in phosphate binder therapy
caution_foods.action: No strict avoidance necessary; variety in vegetable intake is acceptable

caution_foods.name: Whole grains and fiber-rich foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Phytates in whole grains can bind calcium, slightly reducing absorption
caution_foods.action: Adequate spacing between calcium acetate and high-phytate meals is reasonable

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum calcium, phosphorus, and parathyroid hormone levels regularly in patients with chronic kidney disease. Assess for signs of hypercalcemia (nausea, vomiting, constipation, lethargy) and ensure compliance with dietary phosphorus restriction for optimal therapeutic outcome.
